intended_object: The canonical injective homomorphism W_K → G_K from the local Weil group of a nonarchimedean local field K to its absolute Galois group, as in Tate's "Number theoretic background", §1.4. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`WeilGroup K` is a type synonym for the subgroup `localWeilGroup K` of `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K`. That subgroup is the preimage of the integer powers of arithmetic Frobenius under restriction to K^{ur}, which is the standard definition of W_K. `weilToAbsolute` is the subgroup inclusion `(localWeilGroup K).subtype`, seen as a group homomorphism `WeilGroup K →* G_K`. This is exactly the natural inclusion W_K ↪ G_K (the map r in Tate's notation).

At this point it is only a group homomorphism, not a continuous one. That is fine: the module says the topology on `WeilGroup K` is deliberately not the subspace topology. Even so, the map is the right one as a map of groups.

The setting (a nonarchimedean local field) is the one in which the local Weil group is defined, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no Weil group.
